title: WorldBench: Evaluating LLMs on Three.js Voxel World Generation
display: A benchmark and judge that explores and reads LLM-written 3D worlds
summary: Language models can now write whole interactive 3D worlds as code, but grading them automatically is unreliable: a judge that only looks at screenshots, or only reads the source, misses a lot. WorldBench gives every model one prompt describing a floating voxel island with ten biomes, physics, and day/night and seasonal cycles. Its judge explores the running world and reads the code, and trusts neither on its own: a code quote only counts if the file really contains it, and visual claims are checked against measured pixels. In a mutation test, code-only judging still gave full credit to four of five deliberately removed features; WorldBench cuts the points kept on removed features by a third.
